title.narrative: Output 3.2. Increased capacity of Member States to formulate and implement policies and strategies for creating decent work in the rural economy

description.narrative:
A national compliance model in the agriculture sector was developed and validated by tripartite constituents to advance decent work in the sector. Its implementation started through outreach and capacity development of farm owners, farmers and on-farm workers. A Code of Conduct for Fair Recruitment was developed on a tripartite basis to protect agricultural workers, including in the Kurdistan region, against fraudulent and abusive recruitment practices. Decent job opportunities in rural areas were improved through Employment-Intensive Investment interventions in collaboration with local stakeholders. EIIP focused on using local resource-based technologies for public infrastructure, prioritizing decent working conditions and skill development for local community members and displaced people. Rural interventions in Basra and Dohuk governorates improved agricultural productivity, gender-sensitive rural entrepreneurship, and employment services’ outreach: 522 people (180 youth and 100 women) were trained on improved agricultural practices; 500 women agricultural workers enhanced their business skills and were enabled to access on-farm opportunities; 55 members of agricultural cooperatives (16 women and 12 youth) were trained in improved human resource management and farm management practices; 108 potential entrepreneurs from rural areas followed a comprehensive business management training; 2,082 individuals benefitted from training on fair recruitment in agriculture; 2,043 agricultural workers ( 1,191 women, 1,631 youth, and 13 people with disabilities) benefited from improved employment services in rural areas; 23 Employment Service Centre Officers (14 women) were trained to better address the unique needs of agricultural workers and improve the outreach of these services 5 farms received tailored sessions about employment services in agriculture; 2 employment service packages were developed, targeting youth, women, people with disabilities and refugees The ILO supported the conduct of a series of meetings and round table discussions aimed at developing, reviewing and validating the national compliance model in the agriculture sector. These consultative meetings involved a total of 43 participants (including 13 women) representing ILO's tripartite constituents. The ILO, with the support of the European Union provided technical support to tripartite constituents for the development of the Code of Conduct for Fair Recruitment in the agriculture sector, including through a series of validation workshops.
The ILO, with support from the European Union (EU) has provided technical support for the capacity development of constituents, building on ILO relevant tools ILO's General Principles and Operational Guidelines on Fair Recruitment; Gender and Entrepreneurship Together (GETAhead), Start and Improve Your Business (SIYB), ILO’s Think.Coop and Start.Coop global learning tools).

Output 2.4. Increased capacity Member States to apply sectoral international labour standards, codes of practice and guidelines

description.narrative:
The Government of Kurdistan Region (KRG) of Iraq adopted ILO’s Employment Intensive Investment Programme (EIIP) approach in selected construction sectors where ILO’s sectoral standards and codes of practices and guidelines are adhered.
A total of 219 trainees from different implementing partners were trained on planning, designing, and monitoring EIIP methodology. With the support and contribution of the Government of Netherlands and UN agencies, namely: UNESCO, UNDP and UN-Habitat. The total number of jobs created through the EIIP interventions was 82,157 work days (from 1,460 jobs) were 48% were forced displaced persons and 27% females. The following major activities were accomplished to realize results under this output: Repair works and renovation activities at the Erbil Citadel, and three conservation projects were completed in Duhok as part of the partnership between ILO and UNESCO – Madad project funded by the EU. Furthermore, six projects under PROSPECTS Partnership, namely: irrigation systems improvement for local farmers, solid waste management - compost production and improvement, afforestation works, youth center rehabilitation in Shekhan, and VTC Duhok and VTC Mosel rehabilitation. were implemented in Duhok and Nineveh governorates using EIIP approaches. The initiative also supported 52 young engineers to engage in monitoring the public works implementation. UNDP's cash-for-work projects piloted the integration of ILO's EIIP approach in six interventions in Ninewa governorate. The ILO supported Employment Service Center in Duhok to register a total of 6,145 job seekers (2,597 host community members, 2,941 IDPs, 607 refugees), of which 560 job seekers (299 women, 261 men) have been referred to job and training opportunities. The Employment Service Center in Duhok placed 247 (63 refugees, 78 IDPS, and 111 women) job seekers in jobs. The ILO signed a project agreement with UN-Habitat to integrate EIIP approaches in more than 11 construction activities that are being implemented in three districts of Basra city aimed at creating a total of 400 job opportunities with 37,000 worker days.
